experiment: BGMOWL: what do embeddings add over keyword search on BEIR/SciFact?

dataset.text: title + single space + text; strip outer whitespace
dataset.queries: Retrieve every queries.jsonl query before opening test judgments; then select test query IDs for evaluation only.

bm25.description: Single fixed lexical baseline; no stemming or parameter tuning.

dense.similarity: exact dot product of normalized embeddings (cosine)

ranking.output: full corpus ranking for every available query, TREC TSV compressed with gzip
ranking.ties: descending string document ID, matching pytrec_eval tie order

evaluation.reason: SciFact claim IDs and scientific document IDs are separate namespaces; string collisions do not mean self-retrieval.
evaluation.controls: synthetic perfect, miss, rank2, rank101, multi-relevance, graded relevance controls before real evaluation
evaluation.aggregation: official evaluator macro average rounded to five decimals; also store unrounded per-query values
evaluation.no_tuning: No parameter/model/seed/depth changes after test qrels are read. No train/dev judgments used.

runtime.timing: perf_counter; one unjudged warmup; per-query serial timings include tokenization/encoding and exact score computation/ranking, exclude gzip output I/O; report BM25, dense, fusion-only and end-to-end hybrid
runtime.memory: per-method fresh worker process ru_maxrss; parent bounded polling of RSS as extra evidence; macOS bytes converted to MiB
runtime.index_time: BM25 tokenization + sparse index; dense corpus encoding + matrix construction; model load separately
runtime.truncation: count original document/query token lengths using pinned tokenizer, including special tokens; record counts above 256

resource_gates.pilot: sorted first 128 documents and 8 available query texts; no qrels; stop if limits are exceeded

interpretation.primary: Within this fixed dataset/model/baseline only, compare official metrics, complementary relevant-document retrieval and operational cost.
interpretation.exploratory: Post-result paired query deltas, win/tie/loss counts and descriptive examples; no inferential/general advantage claim.
